subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 2 – Lesson 3: Grammar – could/couldn’t, had to/didn’t have to
outcomes: I can use could and couldn't for ability in the past.
I can use had to and didn't have to for the past.
I can compare life in the past and now.

tf.s: The past of can is could.
The past of have to is had to.
The past of don't have to is doesn't have to.
tf.why: The past is didn't have to.

tf.s: Arlo had to use his brother's computer.
Hanan's grandad's password was Hanan's name and birthday.
Hanan's dad listened to the news on the radio before.
tf.why: He listened to the news on TV before.

tf.s: Hanan's grandma wanted to send an email to Hanan's aunt.
tf.why: Correct! She wanted to email her aunt.

tf.s: Hanan's mum thanked her by buying her a laptop.
tf.why: Her mum read her a story.

tf.s: When Grandma was young, people couldn't write messages on smartphones.
tf.why: Yes, there were no smartphones then.

tf.s: "Had to" means it was not necessary.
tf.why: Had to means it was necessary; didn't have to means not necessary.

boxes.q: The past of don't have to is ___.
boxes.why: don't have to → didn't have to.
His laptop stopped working, so it was necessary.

boxes.q: In the past, children ___ use computers for homework.
boxes.why: There were no computers for them.

boxes.q: She ___ to do her homework now.
___ you swim when you were five?
How did Hanan's dad listen to the news before?
boxes.why: He watched the news on TV.

boxes.q: In the past people had to write ___.
I ___ swim when I was three. I was too young.
boxes.why: Too young means not able: couldn't.

boxes.q: Which device did Hanan's mum use?

mcq.q: What is the past of can't?
What is the past of has to?
What did Hanan's grandma want to do?
o: send an email to Hanan's aunt
read a book on an e-reader
mcq.why: She wanted to email the aunt.

mcq.q: How did Hanan's mum thank her?
o: She gave her a new phone.

mcq.q: Choose: Arlo's laptop stopped working, so he ___ use his brother's computer.
Complete: When Grandma was young, people ___ write messages on smartphones.
Which sentence about the past is correct?
o: In the past people had to write letters.
In the past people has to write letters.
In the past people can write emails.
In the past people have to wrote letters.

mcq.q: Why do we say "He had to use his brother's computer"?
o: Because it was necessary – his laptop stopped working.
mcq.why: Had to shows something was necessary.

mcq.q: Which pair correctly compares the past and now?
o: In the past people couldn't send emails. Now we can send emails.
In the past people could send emails. Now we can't.
In the past people had to send emails. Now we had to write letters.
In the past people can send emails. Now we could.
mcq.why: Couldn't (past) and can (now) show the change.

mcq.q: Which sentence shows that something was NOT necessary in the past?
o: We didn't have to go to school on Friday.
We had to go to school on Friday.
We couldn't go to school on Friday.
We could go to school on Friday.
mcq.why: Didn't have to means it was not necessary.
